subject: Uncommitted IndexedDB active-event scheduler structural assessment
verdict: Draft assessment only; no final source or runtime approval.
positiveFindings: Primitive request closures are dispatched synchronously from native heartbeat success events, addressing the actual timer-continuation inactivity failure. Whole async callback is no longer the scheduling unit.

Container codecs remain upstream; new containers and clear use transaction-owned scheduled store. Index handles recursively scheduled; cursor movement and custom async iteration route through enqueue.

Inputs cloned at method call rather than deferred dispatch; immutable IDBKeyRange explicitly exempt. Immediate transaction completion rejection handler, callback failure abort, pending rejection, finally restoration and unchanged serial queue are retained.

For correctly awaited callback operations, callbackPending retains heartbeat through intervening timers; request results resolve callback continuations. No obvious deadlock was identified in that supported path by inspection.

openConcerns.location: scheduled proxy get: nonfunction property returned unchanged
openConcerns.scenario: store.transaction exposes transaction object, and cursor.source exposes an index/store; these provide routes to issue unscheduled operations during an inactive timer. Generic function forwarding also does not constitute a closed supported method set.
openConcerns.requiredDisposition: Explicitly close/whitelist facade surface or document and source-check exact supported production accesses; preserve necessary index/cursor metadata without returning unscheduled mutable handles. No claim of complete raw-fallback prevention yet.
openConcerns.status: Structural concern; no browser repro executed.

openConcerns.location: heartbeat onsuccess pending.splice dispatch; stop condition callbackPending || pending.length
openConcerns.scenario: Already-dispatched operation promises are not explicitly tracked. tx.done drains native transaction requests, but JS operation continuations and late enqueue/result errors need explicit testing when callback returns or aborts with work submitted.
openConcerns.requiredDisposition: Prove no false success/unhandled rejection/late work escapes after queue release; track inflight operations if needed. Preserve callback return and original errors, do not silently retry.
openConcerns.status: Evidence gap, not proven failing behavior.

requiredFinalTests: Delayed success/failure and falsy/synchronous callback errors in actual browser, all live and reopen invariants.
Every container path including multimap read-modify-write, array size/push/pop, bulk getMany, singleton/set and clear.
Async cursor iteration with timer between yields, continue/advance/continuePrimaryKey/delete/update, early break and request error.
New containers mid-callback remain atomic. Queued second callback cannot enter early; abort drains and rejects pending operations with no writer escape.
Mutable input changed after call must preserve call-time structured clone; IDBKeyRange passes without serialization; relevant invalid-key/request errors preserve behavior.
Actual coordinator late staged-store failure and all persistence/isolation regressions on rebuilt exact SDK.
scopeLimits: Draft remains writable by lead; source hash binds this inspection only and all later changes need review.
No application-store atomicity hold release or historical evidence relabeling.
